facts.title: Science as a group portrait
facts.body: Rembrandt’s Anatomy Lesson (1632) turns a public dissection into drama — Tulp teaches, the surgeons lean in, and the dead man becomes the lesson’s center.

facts.title: The praelector with forceps
facts.body: Dr. Tulp demonstrates the flexor tendons of the arm — authority dressed in black and calm gesture.

facts.title: Adriaen lit like marble
facts.body: The body of the executed criminal Adriaen Adriaenszoon is pale against dark cloth — mortality made sculptural.

facts.title: Seven faces, seven attentions
facts.body: Each surgeon looks differently — at the arm, the book, or us — a chorus of curiosity.

facts.title: Open knowledge at the foot
facts.body: An anatomy folio lies open — text beside flesh, theory beside demonstration.

facts.title: Where the lesson happens
facts.body: The opened forearm is the painting’s brightest argument — Rembrandt’s early mastery of detail and light.

facts.title: Lace against black
facts.body: White ruffs ring the dark coats — civic pride framing scientific spectacle.

facts.title: A theatre of shadow
facts.body: The surrounding dark pushes every face and the pale body forward — anatomy as stagecraft.
